claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm in proof.md can return x with g^x=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.50, using at most 2^130.412656 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) and at most 2^20 bytes of peak total storage. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic, evaluated at the reduced cap 3*ceil(sqrt(r))/2 (heuristic prediction 0.664, declared >= 0.50), supported and limited as explained in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. Total work includes all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, hashing, arithmetic, memory access, recovery, verification and output. The uniform capped instruction bound is (3*ceil(sqrt(r))/2)*163288+2^40, with all costs justified in machine.md (tower-basis Fp12 multiplication at 30,000 instructions, SHA-256 at 20,000, Floyd control at 1,000). No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or actual production-scale attack execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check full-width Montgomery and BN254 invariants, test the actual walk on small prime groups including failures, and reproduce the complete capped cost. These do not prove production success.

title: bn254-gt-dlp bounded small-memory Pollard-rho with tight tower arithmetic
